title: Refactor a Monolithic Program into Functions/Modules
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of refactor a monolithic program into functions/modules.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: Refactoring reorganizes code to improve clarity, structure, and maintainability without intentionally changing its observable behavior. A monolithic program may combine input, calculation, storage, and output in one long block. Refactoring extracts cohesive functions and modules, reduces duplication, and keeps interfaces clear. Tests and comparison help detect unintended behavior changes.
understand.whyItMatters: This project develops the habit of improving structure while preserving correctness.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
Refactoring reorganizes code to improve clarity, structure, and maintainability without intentionally changing its observable behavior. A monolithic program may combine input, calculation, storage, and output in one long block. Refactoring extracts cohesive functions and modules, reduces duplication, and keeps interfaces clear. Tests and comparison help detect unintended behavior changes.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

examples.explanation: Naming responsibilities helps find boundaries for extraction.

examples.title: Keep interfaces clear
examples.explanation: A defined return shape helps callers use extracted code.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Take a short fictional program that reads input, performs a calculation, and prints output. Identify three responsibilities, extract functions, and compare output before and after refactoring.
steps: Take a short fictional program that reads input, performs a calculation, and prints output. Identify three responsibilities, extract functions, and compare output before and after refactoring.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Refactor a small menu or tracker program into functions and modules. Reduce duplication, use clear names, retain behavior, and add or run tests before/after.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
Refactor a small menu or tracker program into functions and modules. Reduce duplication, use clear names, retain behavior, and add or run tests before/after.
Include a short test plan and results.

hints: Change structure, not features, during the refactor.
Name each function after its responsibility.
Avoid creating overly general helpers without a need.
Run existing tests and compare output after each step.
